title: How a Hydraulic Press Works in 60 Seconds 💪🔩 #shorts
description:
A hydraulic press lets a small push create a huge crushing force, an idea Joseph Bramah patented in 1795. Pressure in a trapped liquid spreads equally everywhere (Pascal's principle), so a big piston with 100 times the area of the small one pushes with 100 times the force. The trade-off: the small piston must move 100 times farther. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#hydraulicpress #physics #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A hydraulic press turns a *small push* into a *crushing force*. Joseph Bramah patented it in *1795*.

steps.label: Oil
steps.text: Two pistons sit on the same *sealed tube of oil*, one small and one big.

steps.label: Pascal
steps.text: Push the small piston, and the *pressure spreads equally* through all the oil.

steps.label: Big piston
steps.text: The big piston has *100 times the area*, so it pushes with *100 times the force*.

steps.label: Trade-off
steps.text: The catch: the small piston must travel *100 times farther*.

steps.label: Crush
steps.text: A pump repeats those small strokes, and the ram slowly *crushes* whatever is below.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Push, spread, *multiply*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
